title: One Light Day
one_liner: Ride along with Voyager 1: a live signal delay, a draining power budget and instruments switching off by year.
speaker: Peter Diamandis
context: Peter announced that Voyager 1 passed one light day from Earth after about 49 years. A message now takes a day each way. Its generator makes about 200 watts and loses about 4 a year, and only two instruments remain on.
demo: Visitors press 'Send a command' and watch a pulse travel the scaled distance for a sped-up 24-hour leg, with a countdown and a reply on the way back. A year slider runs the power budget down at the stated rate and switches instruments off as their threshold is crossed. A side chart compares the five-year design life with its actual 50 years, and the craft's speed with the ISS and Parker Solar Probe.
data_plan: A bundled dataset of figures stated on the podcast. The future power path is a straight-line projection of the stated loss rate, and instrument shut-off thresholds are labeled as assumptions.
risks: The stated 200 W may differ from NASA's published power figures, so label it 'as stated on the podcast'. The straight-line projection and shut-off thresholds are simplifications.
